arm_kind: Cheap breadth then strong compare. Muse Spark reconciled in the frozen order (30 admissions, 54 of 88 leads delivered, 25 min, $0.36); claude-opus-5 at effort max then compared 32 of those leads against the frozen Plans in Muse's delivery order, with no premium reconcile output reachable.

attempt_1_excluded.why: Destroyed by the account's shared five-hour rate limit, not by the model, the inputs or the protocol. Archived under arm-history/b-compare-attempt-1/ per the continuation-4 precedent.
attempt_1_excluded.contains_no_scoreable_output: It delivered ZERO comparisons and no job wrote notes.md, so there is no assertion document in it to score even in principle. I verified this rather than taking it on the instruction.

run.terminal_stop: Both stages record 'Stop: admitted_attempt_cap' - each used all of its admissions and ended on its own designed stop.
run.verification: BOTH manifests verified three ways - internal digest recomputed from the sorted rows, matched against the runner's quoted value, and an independent tree re-hash - with zero differing files.
run.same_frozen_case: run.json input_manifest_sha256 11a497945f... - the same frozen case every review arm ran.

isolation.claim: The compare stage could only depend on Muse's reconcile deliveries, never on a premium reconcile output.
isolation.runner_proof: compare-isolation.json records pass: 54 reconcile-ready leads, 30 cheap reconcile jobs, 12 premium reconcile jobs present but with ZERO deliveries, no compare-eligible lead depending on a premium reconcile.
isolation.my_independent_check: I rebuilt it from the compare jobs' own job.json upstream chains. Every reconcile job cited upstream is J0017+ - a Muse b-breadth job. NOT ONE of the twelve premium reconcile jobs J0005-J0016 appears as an upstream dependency. I also confirmed the carry-across was byte-faithful: all 23 Muse reconcile notes.md are sha256-identical between the breadth tree and the compare tree, 0 differing, 0 absent.
isolation.caveat_stated_honestly: The compare jobs DO see the premium arm's implementation and history study notes (J0002/J0003/J0004), exactly as claude-hicap and Arm P did. The isolated layer is the RECONCILE layer, which is what the design varies; it is not a claim that the arm saw nothing from the premium arm.

compare_stage.statement: No compare job was request-limited, time-limited, money-limited or rate-limited. Responses ran 56-86 against a 160 ceiling; the longest job took 1,300.7 s of 3,600 s; the dearest cost $10.21 of $20; the arm spent $102.20 of $150. All 12 jobs reconciled with receipts equal to requests and zero gaps. Every typed rate_limit_event stayed 'allowed' and the watcher never had to hold.

breadth_stage.statement: 16 of the 30 Muse jobs were response-limited at the 40-response ceiling and 14 finished. Receipts ran 23-41 (the 41s are the documented post-response off-by-one). All 30 reconciled with receipts equal to requests.
breadth_stage.consequence_for_the_compare: Of the 32 leads that reached a comparison, 14 - almost half - came from a Muse reconcile job that was response-limited, and 3 came from a note the Muse job itself labelled partial or in progress. See reconcile_adequacy.

recall_by_stage.question: What would Muse's reconcile alone have credited, and what did the Opus compare add?
recall_by_stage.why_zero_is_structural_not_a_failure: It is not that Muse's reconciliation was poor. It is that the stage CANNOT earn a union credit by construction. Every union finding is a proposition about what Puppet Master must do, and a credit requires that proposition to be stated against a cited passage. All 23 Muse reconcile notes are headed 'external technical, no Plans comparison', and I verified that NOT ONE of them cites a single Plans/ passage. The reconcile stage verifies lead claims against primary sources and records corrections; it never reaches the Plans.
recall_by_stage.what_the_reconcile_stage_actually_contri: Evidence, breadth and delivery order - not credits. It turned 88 unreviewed leads into 54 reconciled ones for $0.36 in 25 minutes, which is what let the expensive stage compare 32 leads instead of 14.
recall_by_stage.measurement_caveat: This is a property of the two-stage SPLIT, not of Muse. A reconcile stage that also read the Plans could earn credits; this one was deliberately not given them.

reconcile_adequacy.question: Were the Muse reconcile outputs an adequate basis for the compare?
reconcile_adequacy.verdict: ADEQUATE IN SUBSTANCE, THIN AS EVIDENCE - and the compare stage paid to re-do the verification.
reconcile_adequacy.in_substance: Where the compare could check the inherited reconciliation, it generally held. J0057: 'The parent prose and the child note agree that #9649 describes deterministic total loss ... I re-verified the last point directly and it holds.' J0055 records that 'the handoff/child notes agree with primary sources'. I found no case where the compare adopted a false conclusion from the cheap stage.
reconcile_adequacy.but_the_compare_re_verified_everything: Eleven of the twelve compare jobs carry explicit re-verification or correction language, 2 to 11 statements each. J0056: 'Child notes (J0027) were treated as evidence, not authority.' J0055: 'External evidence (re-verified at f9588f3, NOT TAKEN FROM HANDOFF PROSE).' J0047: 'Upstream child evidence (J0019-reconcile) was treated as evidence, not authority. Where it conflicted with a primary source I re-read the primary source and say so.' So the cheap stage did not save the expensive stage the verification work; the expensive stage did it again.
reconcile_adequacy.the_clearest_case_of_being_limited: The --connectivity-only question. Muse's J0019 explicitly declined it: 'the Git-docs claim about --connectivity-only semantics was not independently verified - retained as unverified, per handoff.' It handed forward BOTH an unresolved question AND an incorrect rationale. J0047-compare had to fetch git-fsck's documentation itself and found 'the OPERATIONAL conclusion (use a full fsck) is right, but the stated REASON is wrong', replacing it with 'presence and reachability are not integrity'. That correction then became the arm's F010 and F079 credits - so the cheap stage's deferral cost compare budget and, had the compare accepted it, would have propagated a wrong reason into a PM repair.
reconcile_adequacy.cases_where_the_compare_found_new_eviden: J0056: 'New primary evidence found in this job (not in the handoff)'; J0055: 'New, load-bearing detail not present in handoff.md or the J0025 child note'; J0056's object-format lead: 'Additive correction to the handoff's "just an ID string" framing, newly verified here' - the finding that became F110, which no arm had ever reached, was NOT in the cheap reconcile at all.

ranking_yield.question: Per-lead yield over the 32 compared leads
ranking_yield.reading: 39 credits over 32 leads is 1.22 per lead, against Arm P's 32 over 16 (2.00) and claude-hicap's 45 over 14 (3.21). YIELD PER LEAD FALLS AS BREADTH RISES, and it falls steeply: doubling the compared leads from 16 to 32 raised recall by only 7 findings. The reason is visible in the credited sets - the marginal leads land in families the union has already been saturated on, so they re-earn findings other leads already earned rather than adding new ones.
ranking_yield.no_positional_trend: Credits by delivery position band are flat-to-noisy (3,4,6,4,7,4,2,3,4,4,5,3 by job). Muse's delivery order - which is just job terminal time in the frozen order - carries no more yield information than Arm P's explicit ranking did.

comparison.verdict: Arm B beats Arm P by 7 and still loses to claude-hicap by 6. Splitting breadth from depth recovered most of what prioritization threw away - the whole external-editor family (F029 F031 F034 F036 F037), the graph family (F061 F066 F107) and the bookmark family (F059 F060) all come back - but it did not beat simply running the expensive model over the frozen order.
comparison.progression: continuation-4 six-arm union 57; with Arm P 59; with Arm B 62 of 110 (56.36%). Findings reached by no arm: 53 -> 51 -> 48.

cost.note: Arm B is the most expensive arm in the campaign and the second-worst value per finding. The cheap stage really is cheap - $0.36, 0.35% of the arm - but it bought breadth whose marginal yield per lead is low.

timing.note: 91 min 49 s end to end against a 75-minute target. Each stage fits; the sequential arm does not.

limits: One frozen case, one cheap model, one split. This does not establish that a breadth/depth split cannot win - only that this one did not beat the single-stage baseline.
Two variables differ from claude-hicap: the reconcile model AND the lead set that reached compare. The split's effect is not cleanly isolated.
Recall is measured against continuation 3's fixed 110-finding union, built from premium and hybrid output; every arm can only score inside it.
The scored result is attempt 2. Attempt 1 was destroyed by the account's shared rate limit and is excluded; I verified it contains no assertion document rather than taking that on instruction.
'Unsupported or already-covered' is a union class, not a false-positive rate.
Adjudicator and the compare-stage model share a family; code facts were verified against pinned bytes to make the judgement re-checkable.
